# The Moon That Hides Its Face

## Scripture

*"When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have set in place, what is mankind that you are mindful of them, human beings that you care for them?"* — Psalm 8:3–4 (NIV)

## Reflection

Step outside on a new moon night and you may think the moon has vanished. No silver crescent, no gentle glow—only darkness where light once hung. But the moon hasn't gone anywhere. It's still there, orbiting faithfully, simply turning its unlit face toward us.

We have seasons like that. Times when God's presence feels hidden, when prayers seem to echo off empty sky. We wonder if He's withdrawn. Yet Scripture reminds us that even when we cannot see the light, the moon remains in its place—and so does the One who set it there.

The moon's phases aren't failure; they're rhythm. God designed them to mark seasons, tides, and time. In the same way, our seasons of waiting and dimness are not abandonment—they're part of His ordering of our lives. David looked at that same sky and felt small, yet he marveled that the God who positioned the moon still cared for him.

If tonight the sky of your soul feels dark, take heart. The moon is still there. The Maker of it is still holding you—whether or not you can see His face.

## Prayer

Father, when Your light feels hidden from my view, anchor my heart in what I know to be true: You have not left. You set the moon in place, and You hold me with the same faithful hand. In seasons of dimness, teach me to trust Your unseen presence. Amen.
